name: vivi-figma-mcp

tools.name: figma_status
tools.description: Which Figma file/page is open in the Vivi plugin and how many nodes are selected. Call it first to check the plugin is connected.

tools.name: figma_selection
tools.description: The nodes currently selected in Figma: their full structure (layout, sizes, colors, text, fonts) as a JSON tree with node ids.

tools.name: figma_outline
tools.description: Top-level frames of the current page (id, name, size, position, child count) — use it to pick what to open with node/screenshot.

tools.name: figma_node
tools.description: Structure of one node and its children as a JSON tree (type, name, sizes, auto-layout, padding, gap, fills, strokes, radius, shadows, text with fonts, component links; vectors/lines carry fill, stroke, strokeWidth, rotation). Every node has box:[x,y,w,h] relative to the requested node. Nodes carry vars (names of bound Figma variables/styles) and asset (photo/icon + export format) where present. Text wrapped only by block width comes as one line with lines:N. Deeper trees are cut by maxNodes/depth.

ids.description: Several nodes in ONE call (up to 10) instead of id: the result is a list, one entry per node, in the same order

compact.description: Drop default values (zero padding/gap, align start/left, name = text). Default true

boxes.description: Add "box":[x,y,w,h] to every node, relative to the requested node (absolute placement). Default true

format.description: json (default): node tree. css: ready HTML with inline flex styles, var(--name, #hex) for variables bound in Figma, :root list, asset placeholders

tools.name: figma_screenshot
tools.description: PNG picture of a node exactly as it looks in Figma (use it to judge visual design: spacing, colors, hierarchy). A tall page is unreadable as one picture: use tiles:N for a sequence of readable slices, or region:[x,y,w,h] to zoom into a part (coordinates from figma_node box).

ids.description: Several nodes in ONE call (up to 8) instead of id: the result is a list, one entry per node, in the same order

scale.description: Explicit scale (overrides maxSize). Use 1–2 for small text

region.description: CROP: [x, y, w, h] in the node's own coordinates (px from its top-left) — a zoomed look at one part (a heading, a card, a form). Default scale fits maxSize, up to 2x

tiles.description: Cut the node into N vertical slices (slightly overlapping) and return N images in order — read a long page in detail instead of one tiny picture

tools.name: figma_search
tools.description: Find nodes by name (or by text content) on the page or inside one frame; filter by type (TEXT, FRAME, COMPONENT, INSTANCE…).

query.description: Substring of the layer name; "*" matches any node (with type)

type.description: Only this node type, e.g. TEXT or FRAME

in.description: Search inside this node id only (default: the whole page)

tools.name: figma_assets
tools.description: List the assets inside a node: photos (image fills) and icons (vectors) with id, name, size and the best export format. Use it before export to get the exact ids. Accepts a node id or a figma.com link with node-id.

id.description: Node id ("12:345", "12-345") or a Figma link with ?node-id=…

ids.description: Several nodes in ONE call (up to 10) instead of id: the result is a list, one entry per node, in the same order

tools.name: figma_export
tools.description: Save nodes as image files (PNG/JPG/SVG/PDF) on disk and return their paths — to use photos and icons from the design in code. Default format: svg for vector icons, png for the rest; raster scale 0.5–4 (default 2). Files are written only inside the current project: <project>/figma-exports by default, or the absolute folder passed as dir (must be inside the project).

ids.description: Node ids (or links with node-id) to export

folder.description: Subfolder name inside the target folder, letters (any language), digits, space, - _ .

dir.description: Absolute target folder INSIDE the current project (e.g. <project>/public/img); anything outside the project is refused. Default: <project>/figma-exports

tools.name: figma_export_assets
tools.description: One call: find every photo and icon inside a node and save them as files (icons as svg, photos as png@2x). Identical images are saved once. Returns the list of assets with paths.

id.description: Node id or Figma link with node-id

kinds.description: Which assets to export, default all

folder.description: Subfolder inside the target folder (letters (any language), digits, space, - _ .)

dir.description: Absolute target folder INSIDE the current project (e.g. <project>/public/img); anything outside the project is refused. Default: <project>/figma-exports

tools.name: figma_tokens
tools.description: Design tokens used inside a node: colors (with usage fill/text/stroke), fonts (family, weight, size, line height), radii, gaps, paddings, shadows — most used first. Use it to write CSS variables.

id.description: Node id or Figma link with node-id

ids.description: Several nodes in ONE call (up to 10) instead of id: the result is a list, one entry per node, in the same order

tools.name: figma_design_system
tools.description: Local styles and variables of the file: color styles, text styles, variables with values, plus the list of components.

tools.name: figma_create
tools.description: Build a design in the open Figma file as REAL nodes (frames, auto-layout, text, shapes, photos, icons) from a JSON spec. One section per call (up to ~80 nodes); returns rootId, node tree with ids, lint issues, warnings and a screenshot. New top-level frames are placed in free space (right of what is already on the page, top-aligned; direction:'below' puts them under it, after:<id> next to a given node, x/y exact) so they never overlap. Use parent to put it inside a container, replace to rebuild an existing node in place. Undo with figma_undo. Stock photos (image.query) are searched on the internet by the keywords. Spec = a tree of nodes, each {"type":...}: frame (layout none|vertical|horizontal, gap, padding [v,h]|[t,r,b,l], align, cross, w/h number|"hug"|"fill", fill "#RRGGBB"|gradient, radius, stroke, strokeWidth, shadow, clip, children), text (text, fontSize, fontWeight regular|medium|semibold|bold, fontFamily, color, align, lineHeight, letterSpacing, textCase, w), rect, ellipse, line, image ({"query":"keywords"} downloads a stock photo; or "path" = a file inside the project; or "data" base64 + "mime"), icon ({"icon":"arrow-right"} Lucide name; "ph:heart" Phosphor if installed), instance ({"component":"<id|name>","overrides":{...}}), shape/bool (vector shapes), and ready blocks: chart (bar/line/area/pie/donut…), table, avatar, logo, qr, barcode, mockup, map — expanded into real layers (editable; change a block's data with update + the block field). Full block fields: figma_guide + figma_schema. Root must be a frame with a numeric w. Auto-layout by default ("hug" + padding), no emoji, real copy. Call figma_guide before the first design — it has the full schema and the design rules. For a NEW page/screen also read figma_guide topics process + taste so it does not look generic.

parent.description: Container node id to insert into (default: the current page)

replace.description: Node id to delete and rebuild from this spec (only for an explicit redesign)

after.description: Place the new frame next to this node (right of it, or below with direction:'below') instead of the default

direction.description: Where free space is taken: right of everything on the page (default) or below it / below 'after'

x.description: Explicit position on the page (needs y too)

file.description: Expected name of the open Figma file (from figma_status): the write is refused if another file is open now

tools.name: figma_edit
tools.description: Change existing nodes with a list of operations run in order: update (fields: name, fill, stroke, radius, shadow, text, fontSize, color, w, h, layout, gap, padding, align…; bulk via "ids":[..] or "match":{in,name,text,type}), move, delete, insert (a full node spec into a parent), duplicate, rename, reorder, restructure (regroup nodes by a target tree), group/ungroup, make_component, combine_variants, rebuild. Ids come from figma_node/figma_outline. An op that creates a node may carry "as":"name" — later ops refer to it as "$name" ("$page" = current page). Returns warnings (failed ops), lint issues, changed trees and a screenshot. See figma_guide for the full op list.

file.description: Expected name of the open Figma file (from figma_status): the write is refused if another file is open now

tools.name: figma_variants
tools.description: Create a Component Set with states in ONE call (button Default/Hover/Pressed, accordion Closed/Open, tab Active/Inactive, size or type variants): "base" is the frame spec of the component (name its text layers, e.g. "Label"), each variant gives props ({"Type":"Primary","State":"Hover"}), optional "set" (fields of the root to change, e.g. {"fill":"#8F430A"}) and "children" (changes by layer name, e.g. {"Label":{"color":"#fff"}}). Components land in the top-level "Components" frame; hover/press/click interactions are wired automatically (Default to Hover, Default to Pressed, or two states click both ways; "none" or an explicit list to change). "replace" swaps loose copies on the page for instances of a chosen variant with text overrides. Same checks and result as figma_edit; undo with figma_undo. Use it for every interactive element and repeated control (see figma_guide process, components).

base.description: Component frame spec; text layers that change should have explicit names

set.description: Fields of the root frame to override for this variant

id.description: Node to replace (a loose copy on the page)

variants.description: Variant to show, default: the first

file.description: Expected name of the open Figma file (from figma_status): the write is refused if another file is open now

tools.name: figma_undo
tools.description: Revert the last N write runs (figma_create / figma_edit calls) made through this plugin: restores changed nodes and removes created ones. Default 1; the last 8 runs are kept.

runs.description: How many recent runs to revert, default 1

file.description: Expected name of the open Figma file (from figma_status): the write is refused if another file is open now

tools.name: figma_styles
tools.description: Create or update (by name) color styles, text styles and variables from design tokens, so a design system exists before building. Then reference them in specs as "style:<name>" (fill, color, stroke) and "textStyle":"<name>" on text nodes. Not covered by figma_undo.

variables.description: Variables in one collection: hex strings become COLOR, numbers FLOAT, booleans BOOLEAN, other strings STRING

file.description: Expected name of the open Figma file (from figma_status): the write is refused if another file is open now

tools.name: figma_componentize
tools.description: Turn 2+ repeated blocks of the SAME structure (e.g. 4 stat cards, 3 list rows) into one main component plus instances: the main component is moved into the top-level "Components" frame (created if missing), and the design keeps ONLY instances that retain their own texts and photos. Run it before you call a design done for every repeated card, row, chip, button, FAQ item, review. ids must be frames; undo with figma_undo.

ids.description: Node ids (or links) of the repeated blocks

file.description: Expected name of the open Figma file (from figma_status): the write is refused if another file is open now

tools.name: figma_fonts
tools.description: Fonts available in Figma: families (optionally filtered by query) and those already used on the page; with family — its available styles (weights). Pick fontFamily for specs from here.

family.description: Return the styles of this family

tools.name: figma_focus
tools.description: Select nodes and scroll/zoom Figma to show them to the user (switches page if needed). Use after building something the user should see.

tools.name: figma_schema
tools.description: Full schema text of rarely used spec parts: "logo", "barcode", "qr", "mockup", "map" (ready blocks), "shapes" (blob/wave/star/polygon/ring/path + boolean ops + masks), "patterns" (texture fills), "grouping" (group/ungroup). Without name lists the names.

name.description: logo | barcode | qr | mockup | map | shapes | patterns | grouping

tools.name: figma_guide
tools.description: Design guide for creating designs: spec = node schema (all fields), craft = sizing + design rules, components = reusing components, edits = workflow and the list of edit operations. Taste layer for NEW pages/screens (read it before designing so results do not look generic): process (order of work: ask, shape, direction, hero first, sweep), taste (what makes a design look designed, reflexes to avoid), typography, layout, imagery, patterns (textures), anatomy (sections per job: book, buy, subscribe...), shapes (21 page shapes), genres, trends (what is current in 2026 and what is fading), composition (make sections unusual: overlaps, absolute placement, shapes; an idea, not a recipe). Read spec and edits (and craft for pages) BEFORE the first figma_create. Without topic returns spec + edits.

topic.description: spec | craft | components | edits | all (these four) | process | taste | typography | layout | imagery | patterns | anatomy | shapes | genres | trends | composition

tools.name: figma_icons
tools.description: Find icon names for {"type":"icon","icon":"<name>"}: Lucide (always) plus Phosphor "ph:", Tabler "tabler:", Material "ms:" when installed. Returns up to 20 matches for a keyword.
